source_text:
Active transport moves a substance against its gradient using energy. Not every active transporter uses ATP directly.

Primary active transport uses ATP directly to power movement across the membrane and establish gradients.

Secondary active transport couples downhill movement of one substance to uphill movement of another, using energy stored in a gradient.

Each sodium-potassium pump cycle uses ATP to export three sodium ions and import two potassium ions against their concentration gradients.
